newsitem.title: USA: U.S. jobless claims rose in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. jobless claims rose in latest week.

text.p: U.S. Labor Department report of initial state jobless benefit claims, seasonally adjusted.
Week Ended Initial Claims 4-Week Avg. Continued Claims
R-Revised, Oct 19 Initial Claims from 320,000; Oct 19 Four-Week Average from 331,250; Oct 12 Continued Claims from 2,429,000 and Oct 5 from 2,516,000.
The department said two states reported increases in initial claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended October 19, the latest period for which the data are available.

They were Michigan with 2,150 additional claims because of layoffs in the automobile industry, an indirect effect of the General Motors Corp strike in Canada, and Mississippi with 1,458, due to layoffs in the apparel, industrial machinery, computer, electrical and transportation equipment industries, and in manufacturing.
Labor said eight states reported decreases in initial claims exceeding 1,000, unadjusted, in the October 19 week.
Among the largest were California, with 5,301 fewer initial claims, Pennsylvania with 4,592, Ohio with 4,046 and Missouri with 2,758.
California cited fewer layoffs in all industries. Pennsylvania had fewer layoffs in the food, service and transportation equipment industries.
Missouri reported fewer layoffs in the construction, trade, service and transportation industries. Ohio had no comment.
